results.title: Standard Chartered plc (via Public) / Standard Chartered advances into digital asset custody offering in Singapore
highlights: Standard Chartered plc (via Public) / Standard Chartered advances into digital asset custody offering in Singapore Standard Chartered advances into digital asset custody offering in Singapore Supporting growing institutional demand for secure, regulated and bank-grade solutions for select crypto and tokenised real-world assets Singapore - Standard Chartered Bank (Singapore) Limited ("the Bank") today announced its plans to provide custody services for selected cryptoassets, stablecoins and tokenised real-world assets to institutional clients and accredited investor corporate clients, subject to applicable regulatory requirements. This move reflects Standard Chartered's continued investment in digital asset capabilities, responding to growing demand from institutional and corporate clients for secure, regulated and bank-grade digital asset custody. The milestone marks another step in Standard Chartered's continued expansion of digital across key international financial centres. Building on presence in markets including the UAE, Luxembourg and Hong Kong, Standard Chartered is extending its across a growing range s position as leading financial and innovation hub makes it an this global strategy. In Singapore, the planned custody service will complement the Bank's broader Financing & Securities Services capabilities, bringing together traditional asset servicing, tokenisation and digital asset custody. This will enable the Bank to expand its support of institutional clients across wider asset lifecycles - from safeguarding and servicing traditional assets today, to tokenising and safeguarding digital assets within an institutional-grade custody framework - through a connected global proposition. Patrick Lee, CEO, Singapore and CEO, ASEAN & South Asia, Standard Chartered, said: "Singapore is an important centre for financial innovation, with a strong institutional ecosystem and growing demand for trusted digital asset solutions. Robust infrastructure will be critical to supporting the secure movement, safekeeping, and servicing of tokenised assets at an institutional scale. This marks a significant milestone as we prepare to bring our digital asset custody capabilities to clients in Singapore. It also reinforces our commitment to supporting the development of a secure and well-regulated digital asset ecosystem in the market." Sharing a Group perspective, Ole Matthiessen, Global Head, Transaction Services & Digital Assets, Standard Chartered, said: "Secure and regulated custody is a critical foundation of the digital asset ecosystem. As a GSIB we provide the trust, security and institutional safeguards needed to support broader market participation and adoption, and we are pleased to bring this capability to Singapore. As client demand continues to grow, we will continue investing in our digital assets capabilities across key financial centres, connecting clients to opportunities through a secure, integrated and globally connected platform."

results.title: Standard Chartered to expand crypto custody services in Singapore
highlights: Standard Chartered to expand crypto custody services in Singapore Standard Chartered to expand crypto custody services in Singapore Standard Chartered's Singapore unit plans to offer custody for selected crypto assets, stablecoins, and tokenized real-world assets to institutional investors. - Standard Chartered’s Singapore unit plans to offer custody for selected crypto assets, stablecoins, and tokenized real-world assets to institutional investors. - The bank said the service would extend its existing crypto custody footprint in the UAE, Luxembourg, and Hong Kong. Standard Chartered's Singapore unit is planning crypto custody for institutions, as it continues to expand its crypto-related services. In a [statement](https://www.sc.com/en/press-release/standard-chartered-advances-into-digital-asset-custody-offering-in-singapore/) released Thursday, the bank said that it plans to offer custody for selected crypto assets, stablecoins, and tokenized real-world assets to institutional investors, subject to applicable regulatory requirements. The bank said the service would extend its existing crypto custody footprint in the UAE, Luxembourg, and Hong Kong. The planned service would come alongside the Singapore unit's financing and securities services, enabling it to "expand its support of institutional clients across wider asset lifecycles," the bank said. "Singapore is an important centre for financial innovation, with a strong institutional ecosystem and growing demand for trusted digital asset solutions," said Patrick Lee, Standard Chartered's CEO for Singapore, ASEAN and South Asia. "Robust infrastructure will be critical to supporting the secure movement, safekeeping, and servicing of tokenised assets at an institutional scale." The expansion follows the bank's move to bring more of its crypto custody operations in-house. In April, Bloomberg [reported](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-04-08/stanchart-weighs-partial-takeover-of-crypto-custodian-zodia) that Standard Chartered was [weighing folding parts of Zodia Custody](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-04-08-standard-chartered-weighs-integrating-zodia-custody-corporate-bank-arm-bloomberg-396692), the institutional custodian it incubated with Northern Trust in 2020, into its corporate bank division. In May, the bank [said](https://www.theblock.co/news/deals/2026-05-18-standard-chartered-absorb-zodia-custody-crypto-business-bloomberg-401663) its non-binding offer had been accepted. Zodia has maintained a presence in Singapore since September 2023, when it [began offering institutional crypto asset services](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2023-09-12-zodia-custody-to-offer-institutional-grade-digital-asset-services-in-singapore-250383) in the city-state. It later expanded into Hong Kong. In June, Zodia [secured a payment institution license in Luxembourg](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-06-09-zodia-custody-secures-luxembourg-payment-institution-license-to-expand-eu-stablecoin-services-404086), enabling it to provide regulated stablecoin custody and transfer services across the EU.

highlights: Particle: Standard Chartered Plans Institutional Digital‑Asset Custody Service in Singapore Standard Chartered Plans Institutional Digital‑Asset Custody Service in Singapore The bank intends to offer bank‑grade safekeeping for selected crypto, stablecoins and tokenized real‑world assets under Singapore’s regulatory rules to meet rising institutional demand. - Standard Chartered, which announced the plan on Thursday, October 8, 2026, said it aims to start the Singapore custody service before 2027 while the offering remains subject to local approvals. - The service will be offered only to institutional clients and corporate clients that qualify as accredited investors and will not include a retail product. - Standard Chartered said the custody capability will sit inside its Financing & Securities Services business, folding regulated crypto custody into the bank’s existing asset‑servicing operations. - The bank is consolidating expertise from Zodia Custody and its internal teams, but its May 2026 agreement to acquire Zodia’s regulated custody business remains subject to customary regulatory approvals and closing conditions. - Regulatory compliance will be central: the bank says client assets will be segregated and carry statutory protections, and the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s licensing, asset segregation and cyber rules will determine which assets and functions the service may support.
